record.context_brief: Confluence transfer for normal conditional systems
record.original_question: Let R be a normal conditional term-rewriting system with conditions s ->! t, where t is a ground normal form of s, and let Rse be the corresponding semi-equational conditional rewrite system with conditions s convertible to t. Under what conditions does confluence of Rse imply confluence of R?

evidence.quote: Under what conditions does confluence of a normal semi-equational conditional term rewriting system imply confluence of the associated oriented system?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A conditional term-rewriting system (CTRS) is a set R of rewrite rules of the form l → r ⇐ c, where c is a conjunction of conditions on terms s, t. Depending on how conditions are interpreted, one distinguishes:

• A semi-equational CTRS R_se, in which a condition s = t in a rule is satisfied when s and t are convertible (s ↔* t) with respect to R_se itself.

• A normal (oriented) CTRS R, in which every condition has the form s →! t with t a ground normal form, and the condition is satisfied when s rewrites in zero or more steps to t using R itself.

Given a normal CTRS R with conditions of the form s →! t (t a ground R-normal form of s), let R_se be the associated semi-equational CTRS obtained by replacing each condition s →! t by the convertibility condition s ↔* t.

A rewrite relation is confluent if whenever u →* v and u →* w, there exists a term q such that v →* q and w →* q.

Problem. Determine general syntactic or semantic conditions on R (e.g., on its rules, conditions, left-linearity, decreasingness, or termination of the underlying rewrite relation) under which confluence of R_se implies confluence of R.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of transferring confluence between semi-equational and oriented/normal conditional term rewriting systems remains an active research topic. Recent work (e.g., Lucas 2024 on confluence of conditional rewriting modulo, and modular confluence studies) provides partial results for restricted classes (orthogonal, decreasing, 2-CTRSs), but no general characterization of when confluence of R_se implies confluence of R is established. The problem appears still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Confluence of Conditional Rewriting Modulo (Lucas)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies confluence in semi-equational, join, and oriented CTRSs, indicating that the precise relationship between these variants is still being developed.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research continues to address confluence across semi-equational and oriented CTRSs, suggesting the general transfer question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Operational Confluence of Conditional Term Rewrite Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses semi-equational, join, and oriented variants of CTRSs and their distinct confluence behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Different condition semantics give genuinely different confluence properties; only partial transfer results are known.

status_evidence.title: Modular Confluence of Conditional Term Rewriting Systems
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for restricted classes, but no general implication is established.
